node.title: Re: To glob or not to glob
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Thank you all very much for the replies so far! (I've /msg'ed everyone to make you aware of this reply-to-all.)

[Laurent_R], [Eily], and [morgon], thank you for your thoughts on recommending [doc://glob|glob]. I'm not sure if there is one true answer as to whether glob can generally be recommended or not - when used properly, it provides nice and short code, while on the other hand, the various caveats can be easily forgotten, and later refactoring of the code could introduce problems, e.g. when a formerly static pattern gets a variable interpolated into it. I guess my emphasis should have been a bit more strong: "it should not be blindly used or recommended."

I would probably say that glob with fixed strings is generally fine, but interpolating variables (especially user-supplied paths at the beginning of the pattern) can get very tricky, and I personally often reach for [mod://Path::Class] in these cases. Another situation in which glob is probably fine is when the user supplies the entire pattern, e.g. as part of a configuration file ("files = ~/foo/*.log"), and one then does @files = glob($config{files}). One can simply point to the documentation of [doc://glob|glob] and [doc://File::Glob] when documenting that configuration option. (The problem of someone overriding glob globally remains, although I wonder how often that might happen...)

[choroba], thank you for the additional caveat, which I've added to the root node. Now that you mention it, I dimly remember this being discussed before, and a bit of super searching found [id://1187638|this thread] with the reference to [https://rt.perl.org/Public/Bug/Display.html?id=123404|RT#123404] - I should have remembered this!

[karlgoethebier], you are quite correct that those modules can also be limited to just one directory, thank you. It feels like a little bit of overkill to use a module like those for a single directory, but then again, it's good to use the tools one knows. My comment was hinting at the fact that I've seen modules like [mod://File::Find] etc. recommended as an alternative to [doc://readdir] without mentioning their recursive behavior.
